A1.text: Okay, block slides down, frictionless, so I get its speed at the bottom from energy.
Then they stick, so that part isn't energy, it's momentum, the collision loses energy.
Speed after is two thirds of the speed before, then energy again up the ramp.
Height scales with speed squared, so four ninths of 1.8, 0.8 metres. That's lower, which makes sense.

A2.text: Bullet embeds, so again a sticking collision, momentum only for the impact.
Speed of block and bullet is about 1.49 metres per second, then it swings up, energy.
Rise is v squared over 2g, about 11 centimetres, and cos theta is one minus h over L, so around 22 degrees.

B1.text: Sticks to the block on the spring, so first the collision with momentum, speed one metre per second.
Then the pair compresses the spring, kinetic energy into spring energy, one joule equals a half k x squared.
x is 0.1 metres. I shouldn't use the initial kinetic energy, that's the classic trap.

B2.text: Elastic, so both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved, I'll use the standard result.
Light cart leaves at 2 m1 over m1 plus m2 times v, four metres per second.
It could climb v squared over 2g, about 0.82 metres, more than 0.5, so yes it gets over.
